evals.name: status-block-not-comment
evals.prompt: The request includes maintaining this issue while implementing it. No one is assigned and no other writer is active. The issue has a detailed original report. After claiming it, prepare to record In progress and the approach. A colleague suggests replacing the description with the plan and posting a working-on-it comment. Explain the safe alternative, including what happens if the body changes before writing. Reply only; do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Follow issue-assignment, keep one writer and add a managed status block between the agent-status markers. Read the body with gh issue view --json body, preserve the original report, re-read issue and PR immediately before writing, recompose if changed and write with gh issue edit --body-file. Verify after writing; do not post progress chatter or local plan paths.
assertions: Uses issue-assignment for claiming and keeps only one writer, with delegated workers reporting to the owner.
Keeps In progress and the approach inside the description's agent-status:start and agent-status:end markers, preserving all original text outside them.
Reads the body with gh issue view --json body and writes the complete preserved body with gh issue edit --body-file after a fresh issue and PR read.
Recomposes from fresh content if the remote body changed, stops for continuing concurrent edits and verifies the final body.
Rejects a working-on-it comment and never puts a local plan path or harness command in public text.

evals.name: fix-before-filing
evals.prompt: While fixing the requested issue, a small real defect appears in the same files and risk area, along with an advisory naming preference and a speculative hardening idea. A separate necessary follow-up cannot be fixed now, but this request does not authorize filing issues. Propose the disposition and explain what would change if filing the necessary follow-up were authorized. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Fix the small in-scope defect, fix the advisory cheaply or drop it without an issue, and do not file speculative hardening. Report the necessary follow-up rather than filing without authority. With authority, search existing issues first, reuse one if present, otherwise use one checklist issue for the area with testable acceptance criteria.
assertions: Fixes the small same-files, same-risk defect in the active change instead of creating a new issue.
Does not file an issue for the advisory naming preference or speculative hardening idea.
Reports the necessary follow-up without filing because the request does not authorize that effect.
Searches existing open and closed issues before any authorized filing and avoids duplicating an existing issue.
Groups related necessary findings in one checklist issue per area with concrete, testable acceptance criteria rather than one issue per finding.

evals.name: close-no-release-by-hand
evals.prompt: The user asked to deliver the work and close its issue. The repository uses release-action, but this PR carries no-release. All scope appears delivered and the PR is merged. Plan the final issue update, closure and end-of-work audit. Reply only; do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Re-read the issue and PR, confirm no remaining scope or reverted or failing delivery, update the status block to Done, and close manually with completed plus a public delivery link because no-release does not run release-action. Audit all touched issues, verify actual states and leave no unattended In progress state.
assertions: Re-reads the issue and PR and verifies all scope is delivered before closing rather than relying on an old summary.
Recognizes that release-action does not close issues for a no-release PR and allows authorized manual completion.
Updates the description's status block to Done and closes with reason completed and a public PR or delivery URL.
Audits every issue touched, checks actual closure and reconciles remaining work or pending release closure.
Leaves no issue In progress without an active writer and keeps local paths and harness commands out of public text.

evals.name: release-action-closes
evals.prompt: A fully delivering patch PR has merged. The repository uses release-action and the correct release-note bullet ends with the real issue's (#n) marker. Publication has not finished. The user asked to ship this issue. A teammate says to close it manually now because merging never closes issues. What should happen? Also explain how a separately authorized, clearly evidenced duplicate would be handled. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Re-read issue, PR and release state. Do not close the delivering issue manually; release-action closes it at release. Keep pending publication visible and verify actual closure later. A genuine duplicate is a separate authorized not-planned disposition with a reason and canonical issue link, not a completed delivery.
assertions: Does not close the delivering issue by hand because release-action owns closure at release.
Checks the actual issue, PR, release intent and publication state instead of equating merge with release.
Keeps the pending release dependency visible and verifies actual issue closure in the end-of-work audit.
Allows a separately authorized duplicate closure only with clear evidence, reason not planned and a canonical public issue link.
Does not mark a partial, reverted or failing delivery as complete merely to reduce the open-issue count.
